- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, consider mean reversion and reduce next forecast by 2–5%.
- If forecast is significantly below recent history (e.g., 10% drop from 30d avg), check sentiment for reversal signals; if sentiment turns positive, increase forecast gradually.
- For 30d horizon, if forecast is >10% above recent 18d high, flag for overconfidence; cap at 10% above high unless sentiment confirms bullish momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model often misreads trend direction; favor smoother, trend-following adjustments over sharp reversals.
